thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 tail latency breach for Emberly (single-tenant) in us-west-2 - started 2276543210. Affected route: /v1/generate (streaming). Auto-escalation to on-call.

oncall-alex: ack - I'm on. patching into the incident now.

maya: seeing a big spike in p99 and streaming stalls. p95 ~ 820ms, p99 ~ 4.1s for the last 4m. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/emberly/streams?from=now-10m

jordan: confirmed high concurrency from their tenant, ramped from 200->1200 concurrent streams over ~3m. Looks like long-prefix reuse + KV cache pressure.

ops-lin: can we reduce routing weight to dedicated pool for Emberly while we investigate? I can flip a policy in the router.

oncall-alex: do it. Move 70% -> fallback pool (lower-capacity cheaper model) and preserve 30% to collect traces.

ops-lin: running command:``` 
# rtrctl set-weight --tenant emberly --route /v1/generate --target fallback-pool --weight 70
OK: weight updated
```

maya: after the routing change p95 ~ 600ms, p99 2.7s but still see streaming stall errors: chunk-delay events where clients see no bytes for 2-3s then burst. Log sample:```json
{"ts":"2276543261","req_id":"r-123","event":"stream_chunk_delay","delay_ms":2400,"stage":"kvcache-lookup"}
```

jordan: that points to prefix/KV cache thrash. Emberly's workload has very long repeated prompts that increase KV footprint. Suggest temporary KV cache TTL bump and increase cache size on us-west-2 nodes by 30%.

eng-sre: can do autoscaling/eviction tweak but need a quick mitigation first. Proposing: 1) increase in-memory KV cap for emberly-worker pool, 2) enable per-tenant aggressive prefix eviction, 3) short-lived reroute (already done). I can apply (1) now.

ops-lin: applying kvcap change:```
# k8s exec -n runtime emberly-worker-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'env REDWOOD_KV_MAX_ITEMS=130000 && supervisorctl restart worker'
restart: worker: SUCCESS
```

maya: monitoring... p99 dropped to ~1.6s after the kvcap bump, streaming stall events down 80% in logs. Still some residual 1-1.5s tail for certain long-prefix prompts.

customer-success-ella: Emberly reports interactive notebook sessions are lagging for a subset of users — they estimate ~8% of sessions saw >5s stalls during the spike. They're on call with our CS shift. No data exfiltration; purely latency.

jordan: note - model variant mismatch on fallback pool caused slight quality regression for some requests; CS FYI so they can set expectations.

eng-sre: rolling a targeted canary patch that tightens KV eviction threshold for long-prefix detection and reduces kv lookups per request for repeated prefixes. Canary to 5% traffic for 10m, then 25%.

ops-lin: canary command:```
# rollout put canary --service emberly-worker --image sha:ab12 --traffic 5%
Canary started
```

maya: metrics during canary (5m window): p99 1.3s, streaming-stall events near baseline. No error spike. Increasing to 25% now.

eng-sre: 25% stable. We'll keep 25% for 15m and then promote if no regressions. Logging shows prefix-hit ratio improved ~22% after the change.

oncall-alex: summary for now: - Immediate routing weight change reduced load on main pool. - KV cap bump gave quick p99 improvement. - Canary patch further reduced stalls. Customer impact: degraded interactive experience for ~8% of sessions for ~18m. Severity set to SEV2.

customer-success-ella: Emberly appreciates the interim fixes. They request a post-incident timeline and rollback plan if the patch affects quality.

jordan: assigning follow-ups: 1) eng-sre to own postmortem and root-cause (owner: jordan), 2) runtime to run longer-term KV sizing for tenant hotspots (owner: eng-sre), 3) product to discuss per-tenant cache limits/quotas (owner: maya).

eng-sre: I'll drop links to the traces and flamegraphs in the postmortem doc and include a replay script to reproduce the long-prefix workload.

oncall-alex: handing off to night on-call @oncall-jen at 2276543400. Jen, incident is stable but still in monitoring. Please escalate if p99 > 2s again.

oncall-jen: acked. I'll keep an eye for next 3 hours and collect logs for postmortem.

oncall-alex: closing this active thread. Filing incident record and tagging SEV2. Thanks all for quick moves.
